title: Qualcomm and Arm jury to return next week after deliberations in contract dispute case
source_used: Reuters headline plus Reuters' same-day trial preview (Yahoo Finance copy) and Tech Times
key_facts: Reuters headline: the Qualcomm and Arm jury will return next week after deliberations in the contract dispute.
Qualcomm's lawsuit against Arm went to a jury in Wilmington, Delaware on Friday 9 Oct 2026 after a five-day trial.
Qualcomm says Arm breached licensing agreements by withholding software patches and tools and by violating a clause meant to keep Qualcomm's price within 10% of Arm's lowest price.
Qualcomm also says Arm tried to torpedo its dealings with Meta Platforms by leaking a 2024 letter to Bloomberg alleging a breach.
Arm's lawyers argued Qualcomm suffered no harm and called the suit leverage in licensing talks; a related bench trial on whether Arm negotiates in good faith has no ruling yet.
Qualcomm's licence for Arm's architecture runs until 2033; the judge has not ruled on Qualcomm's request that it could stop paying royalties for five years if Arm breached.
quote_evidence: A lawsuit by chipmaker Qualcomm against chip technology supplier Arm Holdings will head on Friday to a jury charged with determining if Arm breached licensing agreements and intentionally sabotaged some of Qualcomm's dealings with Meta Platforms.

Arm's legal team this week tried to focus the jury on its claim that Qualcomm had not suffered any harm from the allegations in its lawsuit, which Arm cast as an attempt to exert leverage as the two fought over licensing terms.
No verdict had been announced as of publication.
why_it_matters_hint: The case decides whether Arm broke its licence promises to its biggest customer; the verdict has slipped to next week.
notes: Reuters 'return next week' item seen via headline only.
